headline: Tailscale SSH flaw permitted root access via insecure argument handling
summary: Two critical vulnerabilities in Tailscale, including one allowing root access via SSH on Linux and another causing denial of service in Serve/Funnel, have been patched. Users are urged to upgrade to version 1.98.9 or newer.
details: Tailscale has addressed two significant vulnerabilities: one in Tailscale SSH that allowed unauthorized root access on Linux systems, and another in Tailscale Serve and Funnel that could lead to a denial-of-service (DoS) attack. Both issues are resolved in Tailscale version 1.98.9 and newer.

The SSH vulnerability stemmed from insecure command-line argument handling. A user with SSH access to a Linux node could connect with a specially crafted username like "-i", which getent(1) interpreted as a flag, bypassing ACL policies and granting an interactive root session.

The DoS vulnerability affected nodes running Tailscale Serve or Funnel. A single malformed HTTP request, specifically one with a non-absolute path, could cause a CPU core to be indefinitely pinned at 100% utilization, leading to a denial of service.

For Tailscale Serve, this request could originate from any peer on the tailnet. For Tailscale Funnel, any unauthenticated host on the internet could exploit it. Users relying on Tailscale SSH on Linux with autogroup:nonroot restrictions, or running Serve/Funnel, should upgrade immediately.
